question: Can Q167 masked contact and native full-chain dynamics select the N7 quotient from a common symmetric packet?

objects.definition: block dynamics x'=-B1 H y, y'=H B1^T x-B2 z, z'=B2^T y
objects.basis_orientation: A-to-B edges and oriented hexagonal faces

objects.definition: sqrt(N) M^T J, J_e=2 h_e y_e (B1^T x)_e
objects.origin: Q167 local contact current and prior harmonic port
objects.normalization: M=h/sqrt(N), reported P=sqrt(N) M^T J; h columns not orthonormal

sources.source_status: signed support continuity and conditional masked contact internal; mask trigger and material bridge open
exact finite carrier; graphite mapping conditional

assumptions: A1 formal native chain to honeycomb quotient identification, not a measured material coupling
A2 unit full 0/1/2 generator with unchanged B2 under mask; s dimensionless
A3 seed x=e_A0,y=z=0 and externally selected persistent edge e(0,0) closure at both endpoint contacts

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: conserve squared norm and compute exact derivatives
prove all-time free vanishing from invariant seed

technique_plan.technique: integer recurrence and rational Taylor coefficients

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: no material bath, time or force map supplied

factor_origins: binomial derivative convolution and 1/k! Taylor normalization
sqrt(N) reports integer harmonic basis coefficients

clock_receipt.coupling: unit incidence, one prescribed fixed binary gate
clock_receipt.period_claim: finite skew flow is conservative and no irreversible drag is derived

dynamics_readout.state_space: real C0⊕C1⊕C2 on three periodic honeycomb quotients
dynamics_readout.generator_or_update: full skew 0↔1 and 1↔2 incidence; H masks only the 0↔1 contacts
dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: same A0 vertex packet, zero edge/face amplitude; either all contacts open or edge e(0,0) contact closed
dynamics_readout.conservation_and_sources: norm conserved; masked source J is conditional stock injection, not spatial material bond transport
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: free C3-invariant packet projects to zero, chosen edge gate breaks C3 and activates all N

target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: one symmetric packet, two mask cases, previously declared N7/13/19 quotients; exact Taylor orders 1 through 17
target_exposure.selection_criterion: first quotient-dependent term, not fit to angles
target_exposure.baseline: ordinary moiré/PES with full material Hessian and measured dissipation

calculation_steps: Construct B1 and B2 with integer incidence for each N, keeping B2 fixed under H gate.
Verify R_q A_I=A_I R_q on every 0/1/2 basis vector and R_q seed=seed; the harmonic two-dimensional direction basis has no invariant vector.
Iterate exact derivatives A_H^k seed through k=17 and convolve y and B1^T x derivatives with binomial factors to obtain rational coefficients.
Compare exact fractions: all gated series agree through s5; the first differences are s7 for N7/13 and s9 for N13/19.

result.units: native stock flow per dimensionless update, not force
result.precision_and_error: exact integer/Fraction arithmetic to order17; all-time free result by finite representation proof
result.scope: specified finite masked honeycomb carrier and initial packet

verification.method: exact integer recurrence and C3 basis commutation

counterexamples_and_failures: One chosen gate activates all three quotients at first order, so it does not uniquely select seven cells.
Free symmetric linear dynamics never prepare the gate or the harmonic readout from the chosen packet.
A gate mask is an interaction modification and does not claim masked B1H remains a boundary with (B1H)B2=0.
A closed finite skew system has no irreversible Ohmic friction or physical pressure slope.
limitations: gate trigger, timing and persistence are external assumptions
no dimensional material stiffness, damping kernel, force, load or angle mapping
N7/13/19 are selected quotient examples, not measured domain sizes
next_discriminant: Supply a independently testable graphite packet/gate preparation law and material cross-Hessian/bath map, then test held-out angle and load traces.
